answer: Carrier-verified tenure makes sybil attacks costly. Each epoch a tenth of keys must answer a callback to their registered phone; the carrier signs the reply, certifying one verified subscriber held it 18 months. One subscriber holds one key for life; carriers are fined for duplicates, so they verify. Cloned wallets cannot answer a thousand callbacks; those lines are dead. Each identity costs a long-tenured subscription plus the chance a human lifts the receiver, cost scaling with keys, not payout. Detection is a thin ridge of sampling, not a glacier of paperwork, drifting over the dune field.
